title: How the bishop moves
outcomes: Taps every square a bishop can reach, including captures and blocked diagonals
Says why a bishop can never reach a square of the other colour or a square straight ahead

steps.text: The **bishop** moves in diagonals, as far as it likes, and cannot jump. A bishop stays on one colour of square for the whole game: one bishop travels on light squares, the other on dark squares. Captures work just like the rook's.

steps.caption: Four diagonals, but the white pawn on b2 shortens one of them.

steps.text: Before you move a bishop, ask three questions. Is the square on one of its diagonals? Is anything standing between? Whose piece, if any, is on the square? Empty or enemy: allowed, and a captured piece ends the slide. Your own piece: not allowed. A bishop also never changes colour, so a square of the other colour is out of reach for good.

steps.title: Same bishop, one change
steps.prompt: A black pawn stands on f6. Then it becomes White's own pawn. Predict first: can the bishop still go to f6? Then see what a pawn off the diagonal does.
In the silent round, which answers were guesses? Rate how sure you were overall. (low / medium / high)
